reviews.title: Highly Toxic and Dangerous
reviews.text:
Review Title: Major Warning to Parents - Toxic, Dangerous Content for Kids
Do not let your children or teenagers use this app. While it is marketed as a positive motivation or affirmation tool, its content library is packed with highly toxic, psychologically damaging phrases. It actively pushes messages claiming that "being humiliated builds character" and promotes conditional body-shaming by telling users their body is only "perfect" based on strict food choices.
Furthermore, it pushes pseudo-scientific "law of attraction" phrases like "I am attracting people who are ready to respect me." This introduces a toxic victim-blaming mentality, implying that if a child is bullied or mistreated, it is their fault for "attracting" it with their mindset rather than the bully's fault.
It even encourages a chaotic mindset with phrases like "I am the plot twist my own life needed." For vulnerable kids, neurodivergent individuals, or those dealing with trauma, normalizing "plot twists" glorifies unpredictability and spikes anxiety when they actually need safety and stability. This app is filled with dangerous junk science that can trigger eating disorders, severe anxiety, and an acceptance of emotional abuse. Parents, stay away.

reviews.title: Misleading Offer and Cost
reviews.text:
Like others, I downloaded this app with the idea of trying it out before deciding if it was worth my time. Upon opening for the first time, there was about 10 minutes worth of questions I had to answer. As a customer who is curious about the product, getting barraged with personal questions before I can see what this product even is is already a big negative. Like most other companies on the internet, I assume they’re mining my data almost immediately (which is NOT a good feeling). 
Then my biggest problem is the subscription situation. After all those questions I get hit that it’s $70 for the year. There was no explanation on what that entailed (and again I hadn’t even made it to the interface of the actual app yet) and no other subscription options (which turns out there are?!?). They’re lucky I was still curious so I continued, thinking I will annoyingly have to make more time in my schedule just to cancel the subscription, again having to promise my time to something I don’t even know about. Inside the app, I find it mostly interesting and functional. The buttons on the Home Screen are a little confusing on what takes you where. 
Then I go to the subscription section to see what’s going on, thinking I’m going to cancel because $70 is too much. Doing that through Apple brought me to a page with the other options… finally. There are 4 options, none of which have any real explanation of what they are or do other than how much you’re charged per month/year. I notice a $35/yea

reviews.title: Cussing?? And Self-written affirmations no longer read aloud?
reviews.text: I loved this app because I could customize the affirmations that I can play to be read aloud and even add my own so they’re more specific. This was great for falling asleep to affirmations, hearing them and recording them airing my morning routine, etc. I love all the new features and styles in the app, but it no longer reads the self-written affirmations out loud! Huge disruption for me. I hate to be looking at the screen the whole time during the practice. Barely worth using anymore. Going to cancel if that feature doesn’t come back. Also there used to be multiple voice options and now there’s just one voice. Luckily it’s not bad, I just like to explore variety. Please bring back the ability to read self-written affirmations aloud and more voice variety! Also what’s with the random F bomb within the manifesting abundance affirmations?? Very disruptive and inappropriate I feel! Love this app and really want to use it more in the new year. Please update.🤍
